newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish court probes state-Mafia car accident.
newsitem.headline: Turkish court probes state-Mafia car accident.

text.p: A special Turkish court has begun investigating possible Mafia-state links after an accident in which a police official and a wanted gangster were killed in the same car, a court official told Reuters on Thursday.

"We are now investigating the crash in Susurluk," said the official, confirming newspaper reports that Istanbul state security court was looking into the relationship between those in the car with a view to pressing charges of forming an organised crime group.

Former interior minister Mehmet Agar resigned on Friday after the crash, in which a mobster wanted for political killings and drug dealing died in the same car as a senior security official and a former beauty queen.
A Kurdish warlord, Sedat Bucak, who serves as a government MP, was injured in the crash.

Associates say he is suffering from "amnesia". Due to his parliamentary immunity he cannot be questioned against his will, even by the all-powerful state security courts, which deal with serious crimes including terrorism.
MPs voted on Tuesday for a parliamentary investigation into the affair and the Agar's successor, Meral Aksener, has promised the Interior Ministry's own inquiry.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and his deputy Tansu Ciller have denied any link between the crash and the resignation. But Agar said he resigned to clear the way for a parliamentary investigation.
Media reports say Agar stayed in the same hotel as the crash victims in the Aegean resort of Kusadasi shortly before the accident.
